title: Desktop command palette over the command registry
when: A desktop app with many features needs a keyboard launcher that runs any menu command by name, ranks recent ones first and shows each shortcut.
inputs: the command table used by menus
prompt:
Goal: Mod+Shift+P opens a palette that lists every registered command with its group and shortcut, ranks by match quality and recent use, and runs the pick.
Steps:
1. Reuse the menu registry: each entry { id, title, group, keys, when, run }; the palette, menus and shortcuts read the same list.
2. "when" is a function returning false when the command is not available now (no file open); unavailable commands are hidden.
3. Score by: exact prefix of the title, then word starts ("ex pdf" matches "Export to PDF"), then subsequence; ties broken by last used time.
4. Store the last 20 used ids in the settings file and show them first when the query is empty.
5. Typing ">" prefix filters commands; plain text could search open documents if the app has them.
6. Each row shows title, group in muted text and the key hint; Enter runs, Escape closes and returns focus.
7. Run the command after closing the palette so dialogs it opens get focus.
8. Use a <dialog> with a combobox input and a listbox; render rows with textContent.
Quality bar:
- Every menu command is reachable from the palette.
- Opening and filtering feel instant with 300 commands.
Pitfalls:
- A second copy of the command list that drifts from the menus.
- Running before the palette closes, which steals focus.
Verify:
- [ ] Palette reads the shared registry.
- [ ] Recent ids persist across runs.
- [ ] Rows render without innerHTML.
Output: palette.js, palette.css and the registry update.

examples.input: quero um Ctrl+Shift+P pra rodar qualquer comando do meu app desktop
examples.output: Palette over shared command registry, when() filter, recent first, word start scoring, key hints
